approach: A straight line on the displacement-time graph means the slope, which gives the velocity, stays constant, so the motion is uniform.

steps.text: Note the shape of the graph.
steps.equation: The S-t graph is a straight line, so its slope is the same at every point.
steps.why_this_step: A constant slope on an s-t graph means constant velocity, which is the definition of uniform motion.

steps.text: Find the slope using the two points where the line meets the axes.
State the velocity from the slope.
steps.equation: velocity = −2 m/s (magnitude 2 m/s, displacement decreasing with time)

final_answer.value: (a) uniform motion, since the s-t graph is a straight line; (b) velocity = −2 m/s

common_mistakes.text: Taking the slope as 10/5 = 2 m/s without the negative sign misses that displacement is decreasing with time.
Calling the line non-uniform because it decreases confuses a negative constant slope with a changing slope.
